the alpha operon of E. coli is regulated independently of its co-transcribed ribosomes proteins and that the alpha gene is regulated independently of all other cistrons of the operon.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alpha operon is a good example of a novel type of translational coupling, where translation of a gene is regulated by the interaction of a ribosomal protein with the mRNA of a co-transcribed gene.
the alpha operon of E. coli is a novel example of translational coupling in which the translational repression of the alpha gene is uncoupled from that of the co-translated ribosomal protein genes.
